finding_detail.what_is_wrong: The it.each table at line 42 asserts, for every route in migratedRoutes, that the whole file matches /withAdminCapability\(\s*["']logistics\.view["']/ (line 45). Line 52-56 then adds, for the activity route only, that the whole file matches /withAdminCapability\(\s*["']logistics\.manage["']/. Neither assertion is bounded to a handler. Before ADMIN-021 the activity route was GET on logistics.manage and POST on logistics.view, so the file contained both literals; after the repair it is GET on logistics.view and POST on logistics.manage, so the file still contains both literals. The pair of assertions is therefore satisfied by both arrangements and by any future arrangement that contains both strings anywhere in the file.
finding_detail.why_it_matters: This is the same non-discrimination class the ADMIN-021 lane identified in the sibling pin in admin-route-capability-matrix.test.ts, in the same route family, and it is the most plausible reason the ADMIN-016 migration proof reported this route as migrated without noticing the inversion. A migration proof that cannot distinguish the two gate arrangements is not evidence for the ordering it claims to have verified.
finding_detail.example_of_a_false_pass: Putting both withAdminCapability literals in a comment, or moving both into the GET handler, or deleting the POST gate entirely while leaving the string in an import or comment, would all keep this test green.
finding_detail.what_is_already_guarded_elsewhere: Re-inversion is not unguarded today. The POST expectation in __tests__/admin/admin-route-capability-matrix.test.ts:347-348 is tightly bound to the POST marker, __tests__/admin/admin-registry-guard-proof.test.ts compares the declared gate per method against the route source and goes red on a flip, and __tests__/admin/site-map-activity-capability.test.ts proves the behavioural split. This task removes a redundant-but-misleading assertion; it is not closing an open hole.
finding_detail.segment_ownership_evidence: resolveAdminSegmentOwner('__tests__/admin/site-map-route-capability-migration.test.ts') -> admin-logistics, shared: false, include: '__tests__/admin/site-map-' (SEGMENT_OWNERSHIP.yaml:143). The segment is admin-logistics, so no shared_working_set lease is required for this task.
finding_detail.resolved_by: ADMIN-026, 2026-09-28. Resolved and proven: the pristine file passes 27/27 on the inverted arrangement, the per-handler file fails with the GET gate named first. Two corrections to the finding as written, both benign. First, the finding cites lines 45 and 52-56; the whole-file logistics.view assertion at 45 is the one that had to be bounded for the activity row, so the activity row now branches and the other six keep that line verbatim. Second, the finding's example_of_a_false_pass is right for the inverted arrangement and for a comment or import, but a one-sided deletion of one literal does go red on the old whole-file assertion, because the surviving literal vanishes from the file. The non-discriminating case is specifically the arrangement where both literals are present and assigned to the wrong methods, which is what the control now pins.
